lines.trans: Hey you, wait a second, Mathias!
It is not over for Auteuil.
Listen, the situation is becoming too complicated.
I keep you posted tomorrow.
Are you going to give in to blackmail now?
I am a cinema producer now.
You must protect our favorite actors.
I choose the best actor possible.
If Dany leaves ASK, we sink!
The agency will start sinking fast.
I call Franck to arrange everything.
He filters all my recent calls.
Hello Franck? Yes, it is Gabriel here.
Good luck convincing our friend!

examples.text: Cette agence ne représente que des stars.

meanings.note: une agence artistique = a talent agency

examples.text: Ça va? Oui, ça va bien.
examples.trans: How are you? Yes, I'm fine.

meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
ça va? = how are you? / are you okay?

examples.text: Oui, allô? Ça fait des mois que j'attends ton appel!
examples.trans: Yes, hello? I've been waiting for your call for months!

examples.text: Rien n'est signé. On attend l'appel.
examples.trans: Nothing is signed. We're waiting for the call.

meanings.note: un appel de Rio = a call from Rio

examples.text: Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: je peux t'appeler? = can I call you?

examples.text: Ne pleurez pas, on va arranger ça!
examples.trans: Don't cry, we're going to fix this!

meanings.note: on va arranger ça = we'll sort this out
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day

meanings.note: before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel

meanings.en: blackmail, extortion (faire du chantage = to blackmail)
meanings.note: Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'blackmail'.

examples.text: Entre un donneur anonyme et un ami, je choisis l'ami.
examples.trans: Between an anonymous donor and a friend, I choose the friend.

meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to choose'.

examples.trans: Shall we go to the cinema?

examples.text: Elles commencent avec un peu de Botox.
examples.trans: They start with a bit of Botox.

meanings.note: commencer + noun, or commencer à + infinitive

meanings.en: commencer par / avec: to start with

examples.text: Non, je viens d'arriver. Mon père, mais c'est compliqué.
examples.trans: No, I've just arrived. My dad, but it's complicated.

examples.text: Je vais la convaincre de revenir.
examples.trans: I'm going to persuade her to come back.

examples.text: Je vais la convaincre de revenir. J'en suis capable.
examples.trans: I'm going to persuade her to come back. I can do it.

examples.text: Une rivière qui coule? Des animaux qui gambadent dans les bois?
examples.trans: A flowing river? Animals frolicking in the woods?

examples.text: Tout le bureau est au courant?
Donc tout le bureau est au courant?

meanings.en: être au courant = to know about it, to be in the loop
meanings.note: Standard masculine noun meaning 'current; informed (in 'au courant')'.

meanings.en: to yield, to give in, to cede
meanings.note: First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Core French verb meaning 'to yield, to give in'.

examples.text: Je refuse de céder à ses caprices ridicules.
examples.trans: I refuse to give in to his ridiculous whims.

examples.text: La plus grande imprésario de Paris.

meanings.note: je n'ai pas de temps; also before a plural adjective: de mauvaises nouvelles

examples.trans: He wants to become an actor.

examples.text: Line est devenue une star, et Françoise a fait du cinéma d'auteur.
examples.trans: Line became a star, and Françoise made art-house films.

meanings.note: past forms use être: elle est devenue

examples.trans: I have to see the play.

examples.text: Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.en: to leak out, to seep out
meanings.note: laisser filtrer = to let leak out

examples.text: On ne peut pas laisser filtrer cette histoire.
examples.trans: We cannot let this story leak out.

examples.text: On ne peut pas laisser filtrer cette histoire de coup de poing.
examples.trans: We cannot let this punch story get out.

examples.text: Tu es pourrie! Mais c'est fini.
Hé, arrête de me regarder comme ça!
examples.trans: Hey, stop looking at me like that!

meanings.en: hey! (to get someone's attention or protest)
meanings.note: Everyday French interj meaning 'hey!, hey there!'.

examples.text: Laissez vos photos et votre CV ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos and your CV here.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: before the verb: vous la connaissez? les voilà

examples.text: Très bien. Tu peux commencer maintenant?
examples.trans: Very good. Can you start now?

examples.text: Regarde, c'est la meilleure de ses vidéos.
examples.trans: Look, this is the best of his videos.

meanings.note: Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor').
ne ... pas: not; ne ... plus: not anymore; ne ... jamais: never

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.en: pas du tout: not at all

meanings.note: c'est pas possible! = I can't believe it!

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.
C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir

examples.text: Il veut le numéro de Miranda Jones, la productrice de Tarantino.
examples.trans: He wants the number of Miranda Jones, Tarantino's producer.

examples.text: Et Samuel n'est plus là pour vous protéger.
examples.trans: And Samuel is no longer here to protect you.

examples.text: Oui! Mon préféré, Pierre Niney, a un nouveau rôle.
examples.trans: Yes! My favourite, Pierre Niney, has a new part.

meanings.note: also used as a noun: mon préféré = my favourite (one)

examples.text: Elle est partie! Elle m'a quitté.

meanings.en: to leave someone, to break up with
meanings.note: elle m'a quitté = she left me
c'est tout récent = it's very recent

examples.text: Tu t'es endormie en deux secondes.
examples.trans: You fell asleep in two seconds.

examples.text: Si tu veux le rôle, tu dois changer.
examples.trans: If you want the part, you have to change.
If you want, I'll help you.

examples.text: Pour rester à ASK, où la situation est incertaine.
examples.trans: To stay at ASK, where the situation is uncertain.

examples.text: Il faut que cette situation s'arrête tout de suite.
examples.trans: This situation must stop right away.

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.

meanings.note: before the verb; t' before a vowel
used alone, after a preposition, or for emphasis: et toi?, avec toi, toi aussi

examples.text: Ça ne va pas du tout.

meanings.note: oui à tout = yes to everything
plural tous (pronounced 'tous' with s): merci à tous
before a noun: tout le monde = everyone

examples.text: Elle est trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: She's too old for the part.

examples.text: Trop vieille? C'est quoi le rôle, une gamine?
examples.trans: Too old? What's the part, a little girl?

meanings.note: singular and informal: friends, family, children, colleagues of the same age

examples.trans: But I quickly pulled it back.

meanings.note: place: à Paris, à mon cours

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les

examples.text: Écoute, c'est une industrie, et elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: Listen, it's an industry, and it's full of sharks.

meanings.en: écoute = listen, look (to start a point)
